name: Microreactors (transportable nuclear)
principle: Very small nuclear reactors, roughly 1 to 75 MWe, that are fabricated and fuelled in a factory, shipped complete in standard containers and installed on a small site, running for years without on-site refuelling. Designs use heat pipes (Westinghouse eVinci, 5 MWe), high-temperature gas cooling with TRISO fuel (BWXT BANR, 75 MWt) or liquid-metal fast cooling on HALEU (Oklo Aurora, up to 75 MWe). No commercial unit operates yet: the eVinci test reactor reached criticality in September 2026, and Oklo targets commercial operation at Idaho National Laboratory in 2028.

advantages: Years of operation per fuel load with no on-site refuelling
Factory fuelled, so most of the nuclear material never leaves the factory system
Sits on a site under two acres and connects like an industrial plant
Sized for mines, bases and data centres that grid extensions cannot reach economically
limitations: No commercial unit operates yet; every programme is in licensing, test-reactor or demonstration stage
HALEU fuel supply is constrained, and recycled-fuel plans (Oklo) depend on material availability
Cost per kW is expected to stay high at micro scale until fleets are built

notes: The eVinci test reactor is a scaled-down 3 MWt unit at the NRIC DOME test bed in Idaho (DOE approved its preliminary safety design report in June 2025, the first for a microreactor developer). Oklo's INL unit is being built under DOE authorisation, to be converted to an NRC commercial licence. The US Army selected eVinci for the next phase of its Janus programme in August 2026 (energy.gov article read 26 October 2026).
